AutoGluon-TimeSeries (AG-TS) extends AutoML principles to probabilistic time series forecasting using a diverse model zoo and greedy ensemble selection. It optimizes weighted quantile loss (wQL) and mean absolute scaled error (MASE) for point and interval forecasts. The system supports panel time series with optional static and time-varying covariates, predicting both mean and quantile forecasts. Its validation strategy employs time-series cross-validation (TS-CV) with rolling origins, ensuring temporal consistency. The core innovation lies in automated probabilistic forecasting, where quantile outputs enable GSI's Bayesian inference pipelines and GSE's state transition modeling. The ensemble mechanism assumes model diversity enhances forecast robustness, while the use of known-future covariates allows for dynamic feature integration. The framework's modular design enables direct reuse in GSE for team strength trajectory modeling, where quantiles define win probability distributions.
